summary: Full end-to-end verification of the newly added $12 CAD Stripe deposit flow for Ajay Haircut. Backend: 14/14 pytest cases pass covering checkout creation, Tuesday rejection (400), slot-collision (409), invalid slot (400), status polling for unpaid session (unpaid + booking=null + amount_total=1200 + currency='cad'), idempotency across multiple status polls, and regression on /api/bookings, /api/bookings/availability, /api/contact, /api/. Frontend: drove a real Stripe hosted checkout with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 — session created, payment submitted, redirect back to site with ?session_id=... auto-opened dialog in polling mode and transitioned to 'Booking Confirmed!' with $12 CAD deposit shown; booking appeared in GET /api/bookings with deposit_paid=12.0; two subsequent status polls returned payment_status='paid' with the same booking and NO duplicate was created (idempotency verified). Frontend UI flow (step1 service -> step2 date+slot -> step3 info -> step4 deposit -> Pay $12 Deposit) redirects to checkout.stripe.com correctly. Tuesday selection in Step2 shows 'booking-closed' text and renders 0 slot buttons.
critical_code_review_comments: Slot-collision check in /api/bookings/checkout is race-prone: two concurrent checkouts for same (date,time) can both create Stripe sessions since the DB uniqueness only fires when the actual booking is inserted post-payment. Only one will succeed at _finalize_booking (still fine because bookings are idempotency-guarded per session), but the loser will lose their deposit-attempt UX. Consider a unique index on (date,time) in db.bookings and/or reserving the slot pre-payment with a short TTL doc.

/api/bookings still allows direct booking creation without deposit (bypasses payment). This endpoint should either be admin-gated, removed, or documented as internal-only — otherwise the new deposit gate is optional in practice.

_process_paid_session uses `processed` flag for idempotency but there is no unique index on payment_transactions.session_id, so a rare double-insert path could break the guarantee. Add: db.payment_transactions.create_index('session_id', unique=True).
checkout_status writes status updates to the DB even for unpaid polls — high-frequency polling from the browser will cause churn. A short-circuit when already 'paid' would help.
Fallback for STRIPE_API_KEY missing raises 500 in checkout — fine, but the same code path is hit inside webhook / status; consider centralizing the check.
No unit test coverage of the webhook path (POST /api/webhook/stripe) — signature verification only exercised at runtime by Stripe.
Radix Dialog a11y warnings from iteration_1 were fixed (sr-only DialogTitle + DialogDescription now present).
test_credentials: No auth. Stripe test card 4242 4242 4242 4242, any future expiry, CVC 123. Recipient email delivered@resend.dev.
seed_data_creation: Created ~5 TEST_ payment_transactions rows (mostly unpaid/initiated) and 2 TEST_ bookings (one paid via real Stripe test flow with deposit_paid=12.0, one direct via /api/bookings) plus 1 TEST_ContactDep entry.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite at /app/backend/tests/ (backend_test.py + test_payments.py) — 14 tests total. test_payments.py covers the Stripe deposit contract without needing a real card. Full paid-flow was executed manually via Playwright driving checkout.stripe.com and verified booking appears + idempotent status polling. If retesting the paid flow, reuse the same Playwright script (viewport 1920x1080, wait 3s after goto to Stripe, fill cardNumber/cardExpiry/cardCvc/billingName, submit, wait_for_url '**?session_id=**', then wait for [data-testid=booking-confirmation]).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Iteration_1 tests had 2 stale assertions (slot count 11 vs actual 12, and a deterministic future_date that hit an already-booked slot from prior runs) which were fixed test-side.
